tree: If your automation renewal falls in the first half of 2027, the useful work happens now, before the quote arrives. Here are ten questions to answer first. Most can be answered from data you already have.
How many licensed bots ran in the last 30 days? The gap between licensed and active is often the first saving.
Which ten bots broke most often this year, and why? Look for patterns: the same portal, the same application, the same upgrade cycle.
What did break-fix cost? Count CoE hours and contractor spend, not only tickets.
How long does a typical fix take, from failure to green? Every hour of that is work that went to a person.
About the work bots hand back
How many items do bots hand to people each month? Ask operations, not the CoE.
Which queue is biggest? One queue with more than 1,000 items a month is a good place to test something new.
What makes those items exceptions? Odd formats, missing data, a judgment call, or a screen the bot can't read? The answer tells you what would fix it.
What's on the roadmap that the current approach can't reach? Citrix, desktop applications and third-party portals are common gaps.
What would security need to approve a new approach? Find out now, not in March.
Can we test an alternative on one process before we sign? A two-week test on real work is worth more than any slide.
